Feature: Is there an overt marker for the absolutive?
Comment: "Indefinite NPs which are nonspecific may also be marked with taha (indefinite pronoun). Nonspecific absolutive NPs may or may not bear the absolutive marker e."(Seiter 1979: 40)
curated_comment: Overt absolutive: e (common N), a (proper N / pronoun). Table 4 (p.37); ex.72 'Ne fano e tehina...', 'Hopo hifo a lautolu'. Paradigm (Seiter Table 4, p.37): ABS e(common)/a(proper-pronoun); ERG he(common)/e(proper-pronoun).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on first person pronouns?
curated_comment: CONFIRMED. 1st person pronoun: ABS a (a au) vs ERG e (e au). Distinct -> ergative alignment. Ex.73c 'To tunu e au e moa' ('I'll cook the chicken', 1SG-ERG e). Table 4 (p.37); pp.28-29.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on second person pronouns?
curated_comment: CONFIRMED. 2nd person pronoun: ABS a (a koe) vs ERG e. Distinct -> ergative. Ex.86b 'Lagona e au a koe' (2SG object ABS a koe); ERG e on pronouns per Table 4 (p.37). pp.28-29.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on third person pronouns?
curated_comment: CONFIRMED. 3rd person pronoun: ABS a (a ia, a lautolu) vs ERG e (e ia). Distinct -> ergative. Ex.86c 'fakavihia e ia a Pulevaka' (3SG-ERG e ia); ex.72c 'a lautolu' (3PL-ABS). Table 4 (p.37); pp.28-29,49.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on full NPs?
curated_comment: CONFIRMED. Common N: ABS e vs ERG he. Distinct -> ergative. Ex.73a 'Ne kai he pusi ia e moa' (cat-ERG he ... chicken-ABS e). Table 4 (p.37); pp.28-37.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the imperfective aspect?
curated_comment: No aspectual split: ergative present in imperfective too. Ergative case is constant across TAM (Niuean is a non-split syntactic-ergative language). pp.125-130.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the perfective aspect?
curated_comment: No aspectual split: ergative in perfective (e.g. 'Malona tuai e kapiniu' Perf; 'Kua fakavihia e ia...' Perf, ex.86c). pp.125-130.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the past tense?
curated_comment: Past tense: ergative present (ex.73a 'Ne kai he pusi... e moa', Pst). No tense split.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-past tenses?
Comment: “Niuean … is a strict VSO language with an ergative system of case marking.” (Seiter 1979: 1)
curated_comment: Non-past: ergative present in future ('To tunu e au...', ex.73c) and present ('Ko e tele e Sione a Sefa', ex.73d). No tense split.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the indicative mood?
curated_comment: Indicative: ergative present in declaratives (ex.73). p.29.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-indicative moods?
curated_comment: No mood split: ergative is constant (syntactic ergativity, not mood-conditioned). p.5.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the realis status?
curated_comment: Realis: ergative present in realis declaratives. p.29.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the irrealis status?
curated_comment: No status split: ergative constant. p.29.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an agentive A?
curated_comment: Agentive A: ergative (ex.73 cook/eat/help/kick; ex.82a 'fakahu e au e tohi' send-ERG). p.4.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-agentive A?
curated_comment: CONFIRMED (key check). Non-agentive A CAN be ergative: perception/emotion verbs 'see' kitia, 'hear' lagona, 'hate' fakavihia take ERG subjects + ABS objects (ex.86, pp.32-33). Niuean ergative is syntactic, not agentivity-conditioned. NB: many such verbs ALSO allow a middle frame with ABS subject (ex.83,87), but the ergative option exists -> 1. (Contrast Niuafo'ou, where the sketch showed only the middle/absolutive option.)

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a topical A?
curated_comment: No topicality split on ergative case. pp.116-117.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-topical A?
curated_comment: No topicality split. pp.116-118.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an animate A?
curated_comment: Animate A: ergative (e.g. 'he pusi' cat-ERG, 'he ekekafo' doctor-ERG, ex.73). pp.48-50.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an inanimate A?
Comment: Inanimate pronouns are absent, but when inanimate full NPs occur, they follow the same ergative-absolutive pattern.
curated_comment: Inanimate A: no animacy split on ergative; ergative is structural. pp.48-50.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in main clauses?
curated_comment: Main clauses: ergative present (ex.73). p.3.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-main clauses?
curated_comment: Non-main clauses: no clause-type split on ergative. p.4.

Feature: Is ergative alignment of flagging conditioned by any other factor?
Comment: Absolutive marking can drop before au or with nonspecific NPs.
curated_comment: Conditioned by another factor: yes -- the middle/ergative alternation (ex.87) and incompletive-object / pseudo-incorporation phenomena affect core case/transitivity. pp.45-48 (cf. middle objects pp.32-33).

Feature: Are the ergative and the genitive expressed by the same marker?
Comment: he marks both ergative and possessive; distinction via context.
curated_comment: ERG = GEN syncretism for COMMON nouns: he marks both ergative and possessor (Seiter p.37: 'he marks common noun ergatives... and possessors'; Table 4 POSS-common = he). Not syncretic for pronouns/proper (ERG e vs POSS ha/a). =1 under existential reading. pp.121-122.

Feature: Are the ergative and the instrumental/comitative expressed by the same marker?
Comment: Instruments and comitatives use aki e and mo e (absolutive), not ergative he.
curated_comment: ERG (he/e) is DISTINCT from instrumental (aki) and comitative (mo). Table 4 (p.37). Not syncretic -> 0.
